subject: Activation phasing & minimum floor options — Clearmind Dedicated proposal
messages:
From: Peter Chang <peter@clearmind.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@clearmind.ai>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clearmind Dedicated sizing ask and ramp constraints

Jasmine —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. To move this forward with Procurement we need a clear set of options that map to our commercial commitment levels. High level: Clearmind needs predictable 99/95/50ms p95 latency targets for our conversational inference (mix of streaming chat + short completion calls), and we anticipate sustained ~1k qps peak (spikey across 3 US regions).

What we need in the proposal:
- Minimum guaranteed floor (min-GPU) and what that means for latency and throughput
- Typical cluster sizes for the three commitment bands (Pilot, Production, Enterprise)
- Suggested ramp schedule (activation windows and how capacity unlocks)
- Warmup/credits and burst policy during ramp
- Clear rollback/fallback policy if we hit infra limits

Practically: budgetary target is to keep committed baseline under $XXk/mo for first 3 months (we'll give exact numbers to finance once we have a firm proposal). Also want an option that gives us faster time-to-traffic with a low initial commit and predictable step-ups.

Can you put together 2-3 concrete reservation options and the tradeoffs?

—Peter
Peter Chang
CTO, Clearmind AI
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Chang <peter@clearmind.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@clearmind.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-24T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clearmind Dedicated sizing ask and ramp constraints

Peter —

Thanks — attached is a first-draft proposal (CLEARMIND_Redwood_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf). Below are the concrete reservation options and a concise rationale so Procurement and EngOps can align quickly. Ben has been looped in for the technical knobs.

Executive summary (brief):
- Baseline performance target: p95 <= 120ms for 1k qps with continuous batching + KV cache (typical LLM 3k token horizon).
- Recommendation: 3-option structure to match your procurement windows.

Option 1 — Low friction onramp (Pilot):
- Start cluster: 24 A100-equivalent GPUs
- Minimum floor: 8 GPUs reserved (keeps a small guaranteed pool for control-plane critical traffic)
- Ramp: 8 -> 24 over 6 weeks (unlock schedule weekly: +4 GPUs/week)
- Warmup credit: 200 GPU-hours in month 1 to cover load testing and spike validation
- Auto-burst: available up to 40 GPUs for short bursts (subject to regional availability)
- Tradeoffs: fastest time-to-traffic, higher unit cost per token initially, less headroom for sustained 1k qps without burst coordination

Option 2 — Balanced production (Recommended):
- Start cluster: 32 A100-equivalent GPUs
- Minimum floor: 12 GPUs
- Ramp: 12 -> 40 over 12 weeks (phased unlocks: 4 GPUs biweekly first 6 weeks, then 2 GPUs weekly)
- Warmup credit: 500 GPU-hours in month 1 and 250 in month 2
- Auto-burst & priority routing: burst up to 60 GPUs regionally; fallback to quantized variant (model-v1-q4) if capacity constrained
- Tradeoffs: predictable throughput and latency with smoother unit economics

Option 3 — Enterprise runway (Capacity-backed):
- Start cluster: 48 A100-equivalent GPUs
- Minimum floor: 20 GPUs
- Ramp: 20 -> 64 over 16 weeks (staged with guaranteed activation windows)
- Warmup credit: 1,000 GPU-hours month 1 + dedicated onboarding window with ops runbook
- Tradeoffs: best headroom for 24/7 high concurrency; highest upfront commit

Next steps in proposal doc: SLA targets, rollback policy, and mutual action plan (PO milestones, test window, canary). If this aligns I’ll revise the PDF and Ben will add a short operational appendix with batching/KV cache parameters and suggested canary metrics.

Cheers,

Jasmine Liu
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Chang <peter@clearmind.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@clearmind.ai>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-25T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clearmind Dedicated sizing ask and ramp constraints

Adding technical context so we can align on the min-GPU implications. Key points:

- Latency drivers: model size, token horizon, and concurrent KV-cache hits. With persistent KV caching and continuous batching we can often reduce effective GPU load by ~25-40% for conversational traffic with good prefix reuse.

- For the Pilot (24 GPU start), expect p95 ~110-160ms for mixed streaming/completions at moderate batching. At sustained 1k qps you'll need steady-state ~32-40 GPUs unless you rely on burst windows.

- Minimum floor (8 GPUs) is safe for background jobs, orchestration, and a small percentage (~10-15%) of steady traffic — it will not support full production traffic by itself. If Clearmind requires guaranteed p95 at 1k qps even during short windows, the floor needs to be raised to 12-16 GPUs.

- Cost note (very rough): starting with 24 GPUs vs 32 GPUs changes committed spend by ~+33% but reduces need for burst/overage charges. We can model exact numbers once we have your expected token mix and hourly qps distribution.

Operational suggestion: include a 2-week performance validation milestone after the first ramp tranche. We can then adjust batching/window sizes dynamically (we have tooling to push config changes without redeploy).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Peter Chang <peter@clearmind.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@clearmind.ai>
Date: 2026-08-26T08:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clearmind Dedicated sizing ask and ramp constraints

Thanks Jasmine/Ben — this is very helpful. A few clarifications/asks from our side before we escalate to Procurement:

1) Can you show the p95 latency curve (expected) for 8/12/24/32/48 GPUs at 1k qps (even back-of-envelope) so our SREs can sign off?
2) We need a guarantee (or credits) for p95 < 120ms for our user-facing path during Production. If you can’t guarantee it on day 1, we need a canary SLA (7-day) that if missed results in service credits and a remediation plan.
3) For the Pilot option we prefer a lower initial commit (8 or 12 GPUs) but need the ramp to be able to add +8 GPUs within 48 hours if we see early demand.

Also procurement asked for a clean breakdown in the PDF of: committed monthly cost, burst policy pricing, and estimated overage exposure. Can you update the doc and then we’ll circulate?

—Peter
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Chang <peter@clearmind.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clearmind Dedicated sizing ask and ramp constraints

Peter —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached proposal v1 already includes a cost appendix; I’ll circulate a second draft with the p95 curves and the canary SLA language. Quick answers inline and a final two-option ramp we recommend:

Inline:
- p95 curves: we’ll provide a conservative projection table (8/12/24/32/48) using measured throughput from prior customers with similar token mix. Expect step improvements with KV cache effective reuse.
- Canary SLA: we can offer a 7-day canary SLA with predefined remediation (config tuning, priority burst credits, and model-fallback) and service credits if p95 > 120ms for >2 of the 7 days for the production path. Details in revision.
- Pilot activation speed: we can commit to the ability to add +8 GPUs within 48 hours for Pilot customers in the same region (subject to availability windows in the PO). We’ll include a retained-burst buffer in Option 1 to make this smoother.

Final ramp options (short):
Option A — Conservative (Production-first): 12 -> 40 over 16 weeks; guaranteed weekdays activation windows; p95 credit triggers as described.
Option B — Accelerated (Onramp-first): 8 -> 32 over 8 weeks + 300 warmup GPU-hours; retained-burst to guarantee +8 GPUs within 48 hours for first 90 days.

Next steps: I’ll update the PDF with the latency projection table, explicit pricing breakout, and the mutual action plan (Milestone 1: PO signed; Milestone 2: Canary start; Milestone 3: Production unlock). If that looks good, can you confirm the Procurement contact and target approval date?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through the tradeoffs live.

Jasmine Liu
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
